title: Ollie and the Vanishing Water
subtitle: Why does the water go away?
blurb: One sunny morning, the water is gone! Ollie the sea otter has a big question, a speedy seagull has a very silly plan, and wise Gran Mari has a bowl of water and a gentle answer. Will Ollie learn to wait?

spreads.text: One sunny morning, Ollie the sea otter skipped down the sandy beach with his best friend Pip snuggled in his vest pocket, humming a happy little tune. Then Ollie stopped so fast that his tuft popped straight up, because something very big was missing from the beach. The water was gone!

"Where did the water go?" Ollie whispered, holding up his smooth grey wonder rock and gazing at the long, shiny, empty sand. He turned to look right at you with his biggest, roundest eyes and asked, "Why does the water go away?" Then he grinned and said, "Let's find out!"

Down at the tide pools, Gus the seagull landed with a flap and a skid, red sneakers kicking up sand, and squawked, "The sea ran away! Maybe it got bored, or maybe it got hungry!" Pip peeked out of the pocket and did not think seas ever got hungry.

Ollie dashed ahead across the wet sand, his eyes shining and his feet going pitter-patter, until Pip called, "Wait! Bean is still back there!" Ollie skidded to a stop, scooped up his little sister, and said, "Oops, sorry, Bean. Let's go together."

Gus had a faster way, of course, and he was very proud of it. "We'll carry the whole sea back in a bucket!" he said, and he trotted to the faraway waves and back again. But splash after splash, every drop sank into the sand, and the sea stayed far, far away.

Then Gus hurried back for another bucket, and his red sneakers hit a slippery rock. Whoa, whoa, whoaaa! He slid into the pool and sat down in the middle with the bucket on his head, and when Ollie asked if he had slipped, he said, "I did that on purpose!"

The friends climbed the path up to the lighthouse, where Gran Mari sat rocking and knitting in her coral scarf, and she said, "Well now, a soggy seagull and a worried otter. What's all this?" "Gran Mari," asked Ollie, "why does the water go away?"

Gran Mari set a wide bowl of water on the porch rail and said, "This is a pretend ocean, so watch it very slowly." She tilted the bowl just a little, and the water climbed up one side and slid away from the other. "It moves!" gasped Ollie.

Up in the blue morning sky hung a pale, thin moon. "The moon pulls on the sea, just a little, like a very gentle tug," said Gran Mari. "The water rises up the beach, and then it slides back out again, two times every single day."

Ollie spun in a happy circle, hugging his wonder rock, and cried, "The water didn't run away! It's just out for a while!" Luna sparkled while three soft notes rang out, and Gran Mari smiled and asked, "Well now, what do you think happens next?"

Back at the beach, Ollie pushed a driftwood stick into the sand right where the water ended and said, "This is our water line. We wait, and we watch." So the friends built a sandcastle together, taking turns with the bucket while the sun slid slowly lower.

Gus jumped up and cried, "I can't wait any more! I'll go get the sea myself!" until Bean said, "Wait!" and Gus froze with one red sneaker in the air, and then he admitted, "I fibbed before. I'm sorry." Whoosh, the first wave slid up the sand and filled the moat right past the stick.

That night in the Wonder Shed, under the glowing string lights, Ollie opened his four pockets one by one and said, "The moon gently pulls on the sea, and the water goes up and down two times a day. The sea always comes back, if you wait for it." Pip fell fast asleep.

activity_page.heading: Ollie's Wonder Pocket
learned: The moon gently pulls on the sea.
The water goes up and down two times a day.
The sea always comes back. We just have to wait.

try_page.heading: Try it at home!
steps: Put water in a wide bowl and set it on a table.
Tilt the bowl very slowly. Watch the water climb up one side.
Watch it slide away from the other side.
Tilt the bowl back. What happens to the water?
try_page.note: A grown-up can help carry the bowl. This is a pretend ocean: it shows water moving up and down, the way the sea does at the beach.
